passages.text: Some time later, the king of the Ammonites died and was succeeded by his son Hanun.
passages.sermon: The king of the Ammonites died.\r\nHis son Hanun became king after him.
passages.original: וַֽיְהִי֙ אַֽחֲרֵי־ כֵ֔ן וַיָּ֕מָת מֶ֖לֶךְ בְּנֵ֣י עַמּ֑וֹן וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ חָנ֥וּן בְּנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו׃

passages.text: And David said, “I will show kindness to Hanun son of Nahash, just as his father showed kindness to me.” So David sent some of his servants to console Hanun concerning his father. But when they arrived in the land of the Ammonites, the princes of the Ammonites said to Hanun their lord, “Just because David has sent you comforters, do you really believe he is showing respect for your father? Has not David instead sent his servants to explore the city, spy it out, and overthrow it?”
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
Hanun was the son of Nahash.
Nahash had shown kindness to David in the past.
David wanted to show kindness to Hanun.
David said he would show kindness to Hanun, just as Nahash had shown kindness to him.
Hanun’s father, Nahash, had died.
David sent some of his servants to Hanun.
David sent them to comfort Hanun about his father’s death.
David’s servants went to the land of the Ammonites.
The princes of the Ammonites spoke to Hanun, their lord.
They questioned David’s intentions.
They asked Hanun if David really honored his father by sending comforters.
They suggested David had another purpose.
They said David sent his servants to explore the city.
They said David’s servants came to spy on the city.
They said David’s servants came to overthrow the city.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר דָּוִ֜ד אֶעֱשֶׂה־ חֶ֣סֶד׀ עִם־ חָנ֣וּן בֶּן־ נָחָ֗שׁ כַּאֲשֶׁר֩ עָשָׂ֨ה אָבִ֤יו עִמָּדִי֙ חֶ֔סֶד וַיִּשְׁלַ֨ח דָּוִ֧ד לְנַחֲמ֛וֹ בְּיַד־ עֲבָדָ֖יו אֶל־ אָבִ֑יו וַיָּבֹ֙אוּ֙ עַבְדֵ֣י דָוִ֔ד אֶ֖רֶץ בְּנֵ֥י עַמּֽוֹן׃ וַיֹּאמְרוּ֩ שָׂרֵ֨י בְנֵֽי־ עַמּ֜וֹן אֶל־ חָנ֣וּן אֲדֹֽנֵיהֶ֗ם הַֽמְכַבֵּ֨ד דָּוִ֤ד אֶת־ אָבִ֙יךָ֙ בְּעֵינֶ֔יךָ כִּֽי־ שָׁלַ֥ח לְךָ֖ מְנַֽחֲמִ֑ים הֲ֠לוֹא בַּעֲב֞וּר חֲק֤וֹר אֶת־ הָעִיר֙ וּלְרַגְּלָ֣הּ וּלְהָפְכָ֔הּ שָׁלַ֥ח דָּוִ֛ד אֶת־ עֲבָדָ֖יו אֵלֶֽיךָ׃

passages.text: So Hanun took David’s servants, shaved off half of each man’s beard, cut off their garments at the hips, and sent them away.
passages.sermon:
Hanun was the new king of the Ammonites.
David sent his servants to Hanun.
Hanun took David’s servants.
Hanun shaved off half of each man’s beard.
Hanun cut off their garments at the hips.
Hanun sent the servants away.
passages.original: וַיִּקַּ֨ח חָנ֜וּן אֶת־ עַבְדֵ֣י דָוִ֗ד וַיְגַלַּח֙ אֶת־ חֲצִ֣י זְקָנָ֔ם וַיִּכְרֹ֧ת אֶת־ מַדְוֵיהֶ֛ם בַּחֵ֖צִי עַ֣ד שְׁתֽוֹתֵיהֶ֑ם וַֽיְשַׁלְּחֵֽם׃

passages.text: When this was reported to David, he sent messengers to meet the men, since they had been thoroughly humiliated. The king told them, “Stay in Jericho until your beards have grown back, and then return.”
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
People told David what happened to his servants.
David’s servants had been shamed.
David sent messengers to meet his servants.
The men were very humiliated.
The king spoke to them.
He said, “Stay in Jericho.”
He said, “Wait there until your beards grow back.”
He said, “Then you may return.”
passages.original: וַיַּגִּ֤דוּ לְדָוִד֙ וַיִּשְׁלַ֣ח לִקְרָאתָ֔ם כִּֽי־ הָי֥וּ הָאֲנָשִׁ֖ים נִכְלָמִ֣ים מְאֹ֑ד וַיֹּ֤אמֶר הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ שְׁב֣וּ בִֽירֵח֔וֹ עַד־ יְצַמַּ֥ח זְקַנְכֶ֖ם וְשַׁבְתֶּֽם׃

passages.text: When the Ammonites realized that they had become a stench to David, they hired twenty thousand Aramean foot soldiers from Beth-rehob and Zoba, as well as a thousand men from the king of Maacah and twelve thousand men from Tob.
passages.sermon:
The Ammonites saw that David was angry with them.
They realized they had become offensive to David.
The Ammonites decided to prepare for war.
They hired soldiers to help them.
They hired twenty thousand Aramean foot soldiers from Beth-rehob and Zoba.
They also hired one thousand men from the king of Maacah.
They hired twelve thousand men from Tob.
passages.original: וַיִּרְאוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י עַמּ֔וֹן כִּ֥י נִבְאֲשׁ֖וּ בְּדָוִ֑ד וַיִּשְׁלְח֣וּ בְנֵֽי־ עַמּ֡וֹן וַיִּשְׂכְּרוּ֩ אֶת־ אֲרַ֨ם בֵּית־ רְח֜וֹב וְאֶת־ אֲרַ֣ם צוֹבָ֗א עֶשְׂרִ֥ים אֶ֙לֶף֙ רַגְלִ֔י וְאֶת־ מֶ֤לֶךְ מַֽעֲכָה֙ אֶ֣לֶף אִ֔ישׁ וְאִ֣ישׁ ט֔וֹב שְׁנֵים־ עָשָׂ֥ר אֶ֖לֶף אִֽישׁ׃

passages.text: On hearing this, David sent Joab and the entire army of mighty men.
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
David heard what the Ammonites had done.
David acted quickly.
David sent Joab.
Joab was the commander of his army.
David sent the entire army of mighty men with Joab.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁמַ֖ע דָּוִ֑ד וַיִּשְׁלַח֙ אֶת־ יוֹאָ֔ב וְאֵ֥ת כָּל־ הַצָּבָ֖א הַגִּבֹּרִֽים׃

passages.text: The Ammonites marched out and arrayed themselves for battle at the entrance of the city gate, while the Arameans of Zobah and Rehob and the men of Tob and Maacah were by themselves in the open country.
passages.sermon:
The Ammonites were a people who opposed Israel and King David.
The Ammonites marched out from their city.
They prepared for battle at the entrance of the city gate.
The Arameans came from Zobah and Rehob.
The men of Tob and Maacah also came.
The Arameans, the men of Tob, and the men of Maacah stood together.
They stayed by themselves in the open country.
passages.original: וַיֵּֽצְאוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י עַמּ֔וֹן וַיַּעַרְכ֥וּ מִלְחָמָ֖ה פֶּ֣תַח הַשָּׁ֑עַר וַאֲרַ֨ם צוֹבָ֤א וּרְחוֹב֙ וְאִֽישׁ־ ט֣וֹב וּמַֽעֲכָ֔ה לְבַדָּ֖ם בַּשָּׂדֶֽה׃

passages.text: When Joab saw the battle lines before him and behind him, he selected some of the best men of Israel and arrayed them against the Arameans.
passages.sermon:
Joab was the commander of David’s army.
Joab saw the enemy in front of him.
Joab also saw the enemy behind him.
Joab understood that he was surrounded by battle lines.
Joab chose some of the best men from Israel.
Joab arranged these chosen men to face the Arameans.
passages.original: וַיַּ֣רְא יוֹאָ֗ב כִּֽי־ הָיְתָ֤ה אֵלָיו֙ פְּנֵ֣י הַמִּלְחָמָ֔ה מִפָּנִ֖ים וּמֵֽאָח֑וֹר וַיִּבְחַ֗ר מִכֹּל֙ בְּחוּרֵ֣י בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל וַֽיַּעֲרֹ֖ךְ לִקְרַ֥את אֲרָֽם׃

passages.text: And he placed the rest of the forces under the command of his brother Abishai, who arrayed them against the Ammonites.
passages.sermon:
Joab was the commander of Israel’s army.
Joab had a brother named Abishai.
Joab took the rest of the soldiers.
Joab put these soldiers under Abishai’s command.
Abishai led these men.
Abishai arranged the soldiers for battle.
Abishai prepared them to fight against the Ammonites.
passages.original: וְאֵת֙ יֶ֣תֶר הָעָ֔ם נָתַ֕ן בְּיַ֖ד אַבְשַׁ֣י אָחִ֑יו וַֽיַּעֲרֹ֕ךְ לִקְרַ֖את בְּנֵ֥י עַמּֽוֹן׃

passages.text: “If the Arameans are too strong for me,” said Joab, “then you will come to my rescue. And if the Ammonites are too strong for you, then I will come to your rescue.
passages.sermon:
Joab was the commander of Israel’s army.
Joab spoke to his brother Abishai.
Joab said, “If the Arameans are stronger than I am, you must help me.
If the Ammonites are stronger than you, I will help you.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר אִם־ תֶּחֱזַ֤ק אֲרָם֙ מִמֶּ֔נִּי וְהָיִ֥תָה לִּ֖י לִֽישׁוּעָ֑ה וְאִם־ בְּנֵ֤י עַמּוֹן֙ יֶחֱזְק֣וּ מִמְּךָ֔ וְהָלַכְתִּ֖י לְהוֹשִׁ֥יעַֽ לָֽךְ׃

passages.text: Be strong and let us fight bravely for our people and for the cities of our God. May the LORD do what is good in His sight.”
passages.sermon:
Joab was the commander of Israel’s army.
Joab spoke to his troops.
Joab said, “Be strong.”
He said, “Let us show courage.”
He said, “We fight for our people.”
He said, “We fight for the cities of our God.”
He said, “The LORD will do what is good in His sight.”
passages.original: חֲזַ֤ק וְנִתְחַזַּק֙ בְּעַד־ עַמֵּ֔נוּ וּבְעַ֖ד עָרֵ֣י אֱלֹהֵ֑ינוּ וַֽיהוָ֔ה יַעֲשֶׂ֥ה הַטּ֖וֹב בְּעֵינָֽיו׃

passages.text: So Joab and his troops advanced to fight the Arameans, who fled before him.
passages.sermon:
Joab was the commander of Israel’s army.
Joab led his soldiers into battle.
They went to fight the Arameans.
The Arameans saw Joab and his troops.
The Arameans ran away from Joab.
passages.original: וַיִּגַּ֣שׁ יוֹאָ֗ב וְהָעָם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עִמּ֔וֹ לַמִּלְחָמָ֖ה בַּֽאֲרָ֑ם וַיָּנֻ֖סוּ מִפָּנָֽיו׃

passages.text: When the Ammonites saw that the Arameans had fled, they too fled before Abishai, and they entered the city. So Joab returned from fighting against the Ammonites and came to Jerusalem.
passages.sermon:
The Ammonites saw the Arameans flee.
The Ammonites ran away from Abishai.
The Ammonites entered their city.
Joab stopped fighting the Ammonites.
Joab returned to Jerusalem.
passages.original: וּבְנֵ֨י עַמּ֤וֹן רָאוּ֙ כִּי־ נָ֣ס אֲרָ֔ם וַיָּנֻ֙סוּ֙ מִפְּנֵ֣י אֲבִישַׁ֔י וַיָּבֹ֖אוּ הָעִ֑יר וַיָּ֣שָׁב יוֹאָ֗ב מֵעַל֙ בְּנֵ֣י עַמּ֔וֹן וַיָּבֹ֖א יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

passages.text: When the Arameans saw that they had been defeated by Israel, they regrouped.
passages.sermon:
The Arameans fought against Israel.
Israel defeated the Arameans.
The Arameans saw that Israel had defeated them.
The Arameans gathered together again.
passages.original: וַיַּ֣רְא אֲרָ֔ם כִּ֥י נִגַּ֖ף לִפְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיֵּאָסְפ֖וּ יָֽחַד׃

passages.text: Hadadezer sent messengers to bring more Arameans from beyond the Euphrates, and they came to Helam with Shobach the commander of Hadadezer’s army leading them.
passages.sermon:
Hadadezer was a king.
Hadadezer sent messengers.
He called for more Aramean soldiers.
These Arameans lived beyond the Euphrates River.
The Aramean soldiers came to Helam.
Shobach was the commander of Hadadezer’s army.
Shobach led the Aramean soldiers.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁלַ֣ח הֲדַדְעֶ֗זֶר וַיֹּצֵ֤א אֶת־ אֲרָם֙ אֲשֶׁר֙ מֵעֵ֣בֶר הַנָּהָ֔ר וַיָּבֹ֖אוּ חֵילָ֑ם וְשׁוֹבַ֛ךְ שַׂר־ צְבָ֥א הֲדַדְעֶ֖זֶר לִפְנֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: When this was reported to David, he gathered all Israel, crossed the Jordan, and went to Helam. Then the Arameans arrayed themselves against David and fought against him.
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
Someone reported news to David.
David heard the report.
David gathered all the people of Israel.
David led Israel across the Jordan River.
David and Israel came to the city of Helam.
The Arameans were Israel’s enemies.
The Arameans prepared their army to face David.
The Arameans stood ready to fight David.
The Arameans fought against David.
passages.original: וַיֻּגַּ֣ד לְדָוִ֗דס וַיֶּאֱסֹ֤ף אֶת־ כָּל־ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ וַיַּעֲבֹ֣ר אֶת־ הַיַּרְדֵּ֔ן וַיָּבֹ֖א חֵלָ֑אמָה וַיַּעַרְכ֤וּ אֲרָם֙ לִקְרַ֣את דָּוִ֔ד וַיִּלָּחֲמ֖וּ עִמּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: But the Arameans fled before Israel, and David killed seven hundred charioteers and forty thousand foot soldiers. He also struck down Shobach the commander of their army, who died there.
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
The Arameans fought against Israel.
The Arameans saw Israel and ran away.
David and his army chased the Arameans.
David killed seven hundred Aramean charioteers.
David killed forty thousand Aramean foot soldiers.
Shobach was the commander of the Aramean army.
David struck Shobach.
Shobach died there.
passages.original: וַיָּ֣נָס אֲרָם֮ מִפְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵל֒ וַיַּהֲרֹ֨ג דָּוִ֜ד מֵאֲרָ֗ם שְׁבַ֤ע מֵאוֹת֙ רֶ֔כֶב וְאַרְבָּעִ֥ים אֶ֖לֶף פָּרָשִׁ֑ים וְאֵ֨ת שׁוֹבַ֧ךְ שַׂר־ צְבָא֛וֹ הִכָּ֖ה וַיָּ֥מָת שָֽׁם׃

passages.text: When all the kings who were subject to Hadadezer saw that they had been defeated by Israel, they made peace with Israel and became subject to them. So the Arameans were afraid to help the Ammonites anymore.
passages.sermon:
Many kings served Hadadezer.
These kings saw that Israel defeated them.
They made peace with Israel.
They became subjects of Israel.
The Arameans saw this defeat.
The Arameans decided not to help the Ammonites again.
passages.original: וַיִּרְא֨וּ כָֽל־ הַמְּלָכִ֜ים עַבְדֵ֣י הֲדַדְעֶ֗זֶר כִּ֤י נִגְּפוּ֙ לִפְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיַּשְׁלִ֥מוּ אֶת־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל וַיַּֽעַבְד֑וּם וַיִּֽרְא֣וּ אֲרָ֔ם לְהוֹשִׁ֥יעַ ע֖וֹד אֶת־ בְּנֵ֥י עַמּֽוֹן׃פ
